deviations.qemu_behavior: Recalled from QEMU's backends/tpm and hw/tpm sources, not re-read for this entry: the swtpm (tpm-emulator) data socket has no read timeout. A failed exchange is answered by tpm_util_write_fatal_error_response with a 10-byte TPM 1.2-format response (tag 0x00C4, TPM_FAIL), and the next command uses the same socket again. A failed CMD_INIT power cycle during TIS reset is reported and QEMU exits.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: The swtpm data and control sockets have 30 s timeouts. The first I/O error on either socket (timeout, short read, broken pipe) or swtpm response whose declared size is outside 10..=4096 bytes latches the backend failed and prints one stderr line. Neither socket is read or written again: that command and every later one complete through the TIS FIFO with the TPM 2.0 response 80 01 00 00 00 0a 00 00 01 01 (TPM_ST_NO_SESSIONS, TPM_RC_FAILURE), and every later backend reset fails without sending CMD_INIT. Commands refused before any socket I/O (a locality other than 0, a malformed command) fail without latching. When the backend reset for an in-process guest reboot fails, because CMD_INIT was rejected or the backend had already latched, the probe stops through its fatal reset path (a stop line, exit status 1) before any device is reset, instead of panicking.
deviations.impact: A swtpm stall longer than 30 s, which QEMU would wait out, fails the rest of the helper process's TPM commands, and the failure code differs from QEMU's TPM_FAIL. The next in-process guest reboot then stops the VM where QEMU would reboot after a successful CMD_INIT; product runs set BRIDGEVM_EXIT_ON_RESET=1, so a guest reset recreates the helper process and never reaches that path. The guest no longer receives a response that belongs to another command. Evidence is deterministic socket-pair and injected-backend tests only; no real swtpm, Windows or BitLocker run has exercised this behaviour.
